description: Use this when a project needs several icons and has no Family or Set yet, or when the user asks which icon style fits. Not when the project already uses a Streamline Set (stay in it) or has its own icon library (keep it unless the user asks to change). Next: `show_families_preview` with the 3 Families you recommend, each with the `slug` of the Set you choose as `set`. `sampleSets` holds 3 Sets of each Family, best first: the first fits the question best, and its `reasonToRecommend` says why. `whenToUseEachSet` describes every Set of the Family, to choose another when the brief calls for it. When the user asks for specific icons by name, pass them as `userNamedIcons`: the Families that have them come first. Each Set in `sampleSets` then has an `iconCheck`: `found` lists the icons it has, and `noCloseMatch` the ones the search found no close match for. Choose a Family (bundle) for any "which icons should I use" ask: pairing icons with a font or typeface, matching a visual style, tone or brand, or picking between packs. Users say "icon set", "pack" or "bundle" for what this catalog calls a Family — when the level is ambiguous, start here. Answer from results, never from memory: the catalog changes and Family names and slugs cannot be recalled, so a Family you name without calling this tool is invented. Semantic search by meaning (hybrid text + embeddings over family metadata): each result already opens on the Set that fits the question, so no further Set search is needed. Preserve natural-language intent in `query`: full sentences and questions work well, including negatives (e.g. "which families should I avoid …"). Do not collapse into comma-separated keyword stacks unless the user only spoke in keywords — that often drops task context the rankers rely on. Do not elaborate or add preferences (tone, UI goals, style lists) that are not in the user message. For exclusion-style questions, do not stuff inferred positive aesthetic keywords into `query`; emphasize traits the user said to avoid over positives you invented.

limit.description: Maximum number of Families to return (default: 3, max: 10).

productType.description: Only when the user names the product type: "icons", "illustrations" or "elements", or asks for emojis, stickers or backgrounds, which are "elements" even when the user calls them icons. Then only Families of that type are searched. Leave it out otherwise.

query.description: Plain-language user intent. Prefer their full question or sentence (use case, audience, tone, exclusions). Keep negatives and framing (e.g. "Which families should I avoid for a B2B SaaS product?"). Do not rewrite into stacked adjectives or keyword soup (e.g. "B2B SaaS professional clean corporate") unless that is literally what they said. Bad: appending invented clauses like "I want a professional, trustworthy, minimal corporate UI—avoid playful…" when they only asked what to avoid. Good: pass their words as-is; add traits only if the user stated them. For avoid-style asks, keep user-mentioned risky or excluded aesthetics prominent; do not invent excluded traits.

userNamedIcons.description: Optional. The icons the user asked for by name, 4 at most. Write each as the one or two words such an icon would be named, because every word has to match ("bell", not "notification bell icon"). The Families whose style fits are then searched for these icons. Leave it out when the user named no icons: do not add icons you only expect the product to need.
